subproblem.title: Composition of Simon local representations
subproblem.statement: Let n, k, N ∈ ℕ, M, S ⊆ ℝᴺ with S ⊆ M, (V, W, ψ) a C¹ Simon local representation of M with ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ (IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ), V₁ ⊆ V, and (D, V₁, l) a C¹ Simon local representation of ψ⁻¹(S) with l : ℝᵏ → ℝⁿ (IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (ψ⁻¹(S)) D V₁ l). Then there is W₁ ⊆ W with ψ(V₁) = W₁ ∩ M such that (D, W₁, ψ ∘ l) is a C¹ Simon local representation of S (IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 S D W₁ (ψ ∘ l), in particular W₁ is open).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k N : ℕ) (M S : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (D : Set (Rn k)) (V₁ : Set (Rn n)) (l : Rn k → Rn n), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ → S ⊆ M → V₁ ⊆ V → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (ψ ⁻¹' S) D V₁ l → ∃ W₁ : Set (Rn N), W₁ ⊆ W ∧ ψ '' V₁ = W₁ ∩ M ∧ Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 S D W₁ (ψ ∘ l)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof of root.c1_sard-a1, PART II step 7 (choice of W₃ by Simon 4.2), step 8 (image), step 9 (injectivity and injective derivative) and step 10 (properness, the ψ-part), stated for an arbitrary subset S of M and an arbitrary C¹ Simon local representation l of ψ⁻¹(S) inside V. Here a C¹ Simon local representation (Simon 4.1, SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 X V W φ) means: V and W open, φ C¹ on V, φ injective on V, φ(V) = W ∩ X, φ proper relative to (V, W) (V ∩ φ⁻¹(Q) compact for every compact Q ⊆ W), and Dφ(x) injective for every x ∈ V.

1. (Choice of W₁, Simon 4.2.) V₁ is open (it is the target chart of the representation (D, V₁, l)) and V₁ ⊆ V. By Simon (4.2) for the local representation (V, W, ψ) of M (SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter: by relative properness, ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ M, so images of open subsets of V are relatively open in M) there is an open W₁ ⊆ W with ψ(V₁) = W₁ ∩ M.
2. (l maps D into V₁.) l(D) = V₁ ∩ ψ⁻¹(S) ⊆ V₁ ⊆ V.
3. (C¹.) ψ is C¹ on V, l is C¹ on D, and l maps D into V (step 2); hence ψ ∘ l is C¹ on D.
4. (Injective.) l is injective on D, l(D) ⊆ V and ψ is injective on V; hence ψ ∘ l is injective on D.
5. (Image.) (ψ ∘ l)(D) = ψ(l(D)) = ψ(V₁ ∩ ψ⁻¹(S)) = ψ(V₁) ∩ S = (W₁ ∩ M) ∩ S = W₁ ∩ S, using ψ(A ∩ ψ⁻¹B) = ψ(A) ∩ B, step 1 and S ⊆ M.
6. (Properness relative to (D, W₁).) Let Q ⊆ W₁ be compact. (a) Q ⊆ W₁ ⊆ W, so K := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact by the relative properness of ψ. (b) K ⊆ V₁: if x ∈ K then ψ(x) ∈ Q ⊆ W₁ and ψ(x) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M, so ψ(x) ∈ W₁ ∩ M = ψ(V₁), i.e. ψ(x) = ψ(x') with x' ∈ V₁ ⊆ V; injectivity of ψ on V gives x = x' ∈ V₁. (c) D ∩ (ψ ∘ l)⁻¹(Q) = D ∩ l⁻¹(K): for z ∈ D, l(z) ∈ V (step 2), so ψ(l(z)) ∈ Q ⟺ l(z) ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) = K. (d) K is compact and K ⊆ V₁, so D ∩ l⁻¹(K) is compact by the relative properness of l with respect to (D, V₁).
7. (Injective derivative.) Let z ∈ D. Then l(z) ∈ V, V is open and ψ is C¹ on V, so ψ is differentiable at l(z); D is open and l is C¹ on D, so l is differentiable at z. By the chain rule D(ψ ∘ l)(z) = Dψ(l(z)) ∘ Dl(z), a composition of injective linear maps (Dψ is injective on V, Dl is injective on D); hence it is injective.
8. Steps 1 and 3-7 show W₁ ⊆ W, ψ '' V₁ = W₁ ∩ M and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 S D W₁ (ψ ∘ l) (D open by hypothesis, W₁ open by step 1). ∎

```lean
theorem c1_sard_local_representation_comp : ∀ (n k N : ℕ) (M S : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (D : Set (Rn k)) (V₁ : Set (Rn n)) (l : Rn k → Rn n), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ → S ⊆ M → V₁ ⊆ V → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (ψ ⁻¹' S) D V₁ l → ∃ W₁ : Set (Rn N), W₁ ⊆ W ∧ ψ '' V₁ = W₁ ∩ M ∧ Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 S D W₁ (ψ ∘ l) := by
  intro n k N M S V W ψ D V₁ l hψ hSM hV₁V hl
  obtain ⟨hD, hV₁, hlC, hlinj, hlimg, hlprop, hlder⟩ := hl
  obtain ⟨W₁, hW₁, hW₁W, hW₁img⟩ := hψ.exists_open_image_eq_inter hV₁ hV₁V
  have hlD : MapsTo l D V₁ := fun z hz => by
    have : l z ∈ l '' D := ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩
    rw [hlimg] at this; exact this.1
  refine ⟨W₁, hW₁W, hW₁img, hD, hW₁, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact hψ.contDiffOn.comp hlC (hlD.mono_right hV₁V)
  · exact hψ.injOn.comp hlinj (hlD.mono_right hV₁V)
  · rw [image_comp, hlimg, image_inter_preimage, hW₁img, inter_assoc, inter_eq_right.mpr hSM]
  · intro Q hQ hQW₁
    have hK := hψ.isProperOnInto Q hQ (hQW₁.trans hW₁W)
    have hKV₁ : V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' Q ⊆ V₁ := by
      rintro x ⟨hxV, hxQ⟩
      have hxM : ψ x ∈ W ∩ M := by rw [← hψ.image_eq]; exact ⟨x, hxV, rfl⟩
      have : ψ x ∈ ψ '' V₁ := by rw [hW₁img]; exact ⟨hQW₁ hxQ, hxM.2⟩
      obtain ⟨x', hx'V₁, hx'⟩ := this
      rw [← hψ.injOn (hV₁V hx'V₁) hxV hx']
      exact hx'V₁
    have heq : D ∩ (ψ ∘ l) ⁻¹' Q = D ∩ l ⁻¹' (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' Q) := by
      ext z
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hz, hzQ⟩; exact ⟨hz, hV₁V (hlD hz), hzQ⟩
      · rintro ⟨hz, _, hzQ⟩; exact ⟨hz, hzQ⟩
    rw [heq]
    exact hlprop _ hK hKV₁
  · intro z hz
    have hlz : l z ∈ V := hV₁V (hlD hz)
    have hdψ : DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ (l z) :=
      (hψ.contDiffOn.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hψ.isOpen_source.mem_nhds hlz)
    have hdl : DifferentiableAt ℝ l z :=
      (hlC.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hD.mem_nhds hz)
    rw [fderiv_comp z hdψ hdl, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp]
    exact (hψ.injective_fderiv hlz).comp (hlder z hz)
```
proof_key_steps: Simon 4.2 gives an open W₁ ⊆ W with ψ(V₁) = W₁ ∩ M.
ψ ∘ l is C¹ and injective on D because l(D) ⊆ V₁ ⊆ V.
(ψ ∘ l)(D) = ψ(V₁ ∩ ψ⁻¹S) = ψ(V₁) ∩ S = W₁ ∩ S.
Properness: V ∩ ψ⁻¹Q is compact and lies in V₁ (injectivity of ψ), and D ∩ (ψ ∘ l)⁻¹Q = D ∩ l⁻¹(V ∩ ψ⁻¹Q).
D(ψ ∘ l)(z) = Dψ(l z) ∘ Dl(z) is injective.

subproblem.title: Critical parts of almost every fiber are Hᵏ-null (co-area formula with A = C)
subproblem.statement: Assume the frozen co-area formula CoareaFormula (Simon 6.3/6.6). Let N, m, k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝᴺ an (m+k)-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open with M ⊆ U, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on U, and suppose M is a measurable set and x ↦ coareaJacobian M f x is continuous on M. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ, μHE[k](M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {x : coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: CoareaFormula → ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), 0 < k → Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn (m + k)) 1 M → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → MeasurableSet M → ContinuousOn (coareaJacobian M f) M → ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn m)), μHE[k] (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof of root.c1_sard-a1, PART II steps 3-4 (Simon, Ch. 2 §6, p. 66: "An important consequence of 6.3 is that if C = {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0}, then (by using 6.3 with A = C) Hᵏ(C ∩ f⁻¹(y)) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ"). The co-area formula enters only through the hypothesis CoareaFormula (frozen contract definition; in the parent it is supplied by the sibling node coarea_formula), and the measurability of M and continuity of J*f on M are hypotheses (supplied in the parent by submanifold_tangent and jacobian_continuity).

Notation. J*f(x) := coareaJacobian M f x, Z := {x : J*f(x) = 0}, C := M ∩ Z, Hᵏ := μHE[k], Lᵐ := volume on ℝᵐ.

1. (C is measurable.) J*f is continuous on M and {0} ⊆ ℝ is closed, so the relative preimage is relatively closed: there is a closed F₀ ⊆ ℝᴺ with J*f⁻¹{0} ∩ M = F₀ ∩ M (continuousOn_iff_isClosed). Hence C = M ∩ F₀, which is measurable as the intersection of the measurable set M (hypothesis) with the closed, hence Borel, set F₀.
2. (The weight.) Let g := 1_C : ℝᴺ → [0, ∞], the indicator function of C. g is measurable (indicator of a measurable set), hence AEMeasurable for μHE[m+k] restricted to M.
3. (Co-area formula.) CoareaFormula applied to N, m, k, M, U, f, g (its hypotheses 0 < k, IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝ^{m+k}) 1 M, IsOpen U, M ⊆ U, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U and AEMeasurable g hold) gives: (i) I(y) := ∫_{M ∩ f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ defines an AEMeasurable function of y for Lᵐ; (ii) ∫_M g(x)·ofReal(J*f(x)) dH^{m+k}(x) = ∫ I(y) dLᵐ(y).
4. (Left side is 0.) The integrand x ↦ g(x)·ofReal(J*f(x)) vanishes at every x ∈ ℝᴺ: if x ∈ C then J*f(x) = 0 and ofReal 0 = 0; if x ∉ C then g(x) = 0. Hence the left side of (ii) is the integral of 0, so ∫ I dLᵐ = 0.
5. (A.e. vanishing.) I is AEMeasurable and has zero lintegral, so I(y) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y (lintegral_eq_zero_iff').
6. (Identify I.) For every y, since C is measurable, I(y) = ∫ 1_C d(Hᵏ restricted to M ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = Hᵏ(C ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{y})) (lintegral_indicator_one, Measure.restrict_apply). Moreover C ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z, both being {x ∈ M : f(x) = y, J*f(x) = 0}.
7. By steps 5 and 6, for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ, μHE[k](M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) = 0. ∎

Note: CoareaFormula is a Prop-valued def, so the hypothesis `hco : CoareaFormula` is applied directly as `hco N m k M U f g hk hM hU hMU hf hgm`.

```lean
theorem c1_sard_critical_fibers_null : CoareaFormula → ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), 0 < k → Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn (m + k)) 1 M → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → MeasurableSet M → ContinuousOn (coareaJacobian M f) M → ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn m)), μHE[k] (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) = 0 := by
  intro hco N m k M U f hk hM hU hMU hf hMmeas hJ
  obtain ⟨F₀, hF₀, h₀⟩ := continuousOn_iff_isClosed.mp hJ {0} isClosed_singleton
  set C : Set (Rn N) := M ∩ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0} with hCdef
  have hC : C = M ∩ F₀ := by
    ext x; constructor
    · rintro ⟨hxM, hx⟩
      have : x ∈ F₀ ∩ M := h₀ ▸ ⟨hx, hxM⟩
      exact ⟨hxM, this.1⟩
    · rintro ⟨hxM, hx⟩
      have : x ∈ coareaJacobian M f ⁻¹' {0} ∩ M := h₀.symm ▸ ⟨hx, hxM⟩
      exact ⟨hxM, this.1⟩
  have hCmeas : MeasurableSet C := hC ▸ hMmeas.inter hF₀.measurableSet
  set g : Rn N → ℝ≥0∞ := C.indicator 1 with hg
  have hgm : AEMeasurable g (μHE[m + k].restrict M) := (measurable_one.indicator hCmeas).aemeasurable
  obtain ⟨hAEM, hEq⟩ := hco N m k M U f g hk hM hU hMU hf hgm
  have hLHS : (fun x => g x * ENNReal.ofReal (coareaJacobian M f x)) = 0 := by
    funext x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ C
    · have hx2 : coareaJacobian M f x = 0 := hx.2
      simp [hx2]
    · simp [g, hx]
  rw [hLHS] at hEq
  have hEq0 : ∫⁻ y, ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}, g x ∂μHE[k] ∂(volume : Measure (Rn m)) = 0 := by
    rw [← hEq]; exact lintegral_zero
  have hae := (lintegral_eq_zero_iff' hAEM).mp hEq0
  filter_upwards [hae] with y hy
  have hinner : ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}, g x ∂μHE[k] = μHE[k] (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) := by
    rw [lintegral_indicator_one hCmeas, Measure.restrict_apply hCmeas]
    congr 1
    ext x; constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨hxM, hxZ⟩, hxM', hxy⟩; exact ⟨⟨hxM, hxy⟩, hxZ⟩
    · rintro ⟨⟨hxM, hxy⟩, hxZ⟩; exact ⟨⟨hxM, hxZ⟩, hxM, hxy⟩
  rw [← hinner]; exact hy
```
proof_key_steps: C := M ∩ {J*f = 0} = M ∩ F₀ with F₀ closed (continuity of J*f on M), so C is measurable.
Apply CoareaFormula with g = 1_C; the left integrand 1_C · ofReal(J*f) vanishes identically, so ∫ I(y) dy = 0.
I is AEMeasurable with zero integral, so I(y) = 0 for a.e. y (lintegral_eq_zero_iff').
I(y) = μHE[k](C ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{y})) = μHE[k](M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {J*f = 0}).

subproblem.title: Continuity of the coarea Jacobian on M and relative closedness of critical fibers
subproblem.statement: Let N, m ∈ ℕ, M, U ⊆ ℝᴺ with U open and M ⊆ U, and f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on U, and assume x ↦ tangentProjection M x (the orthogonal projection P_x onto T_xM) is continuous on M. Then x ↦ coareaJacobian M f x is continuous on M, and for every y ∈ ℝᵐ there is a closed set F ⊆ ℝᴺ with M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {x : coareaJacobian M f x = 0} = M ∩ F.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M → ContinuousOn (coareaJacobian M f) M ∧ ∀ y : Rn m, ∃ F : Set (Rn N), IsClosed F ∧ M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0} = M ∩ F
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof of root.c1_sard-a1, PART II step 3 (J*f is continuous on M because L_x L_x* = Df(x) P_x Df(x)*) and step 5 (relative closedness of the critical part of a fiber, F := closure). Only the stated hypotheses are used; M need not be a submanifold here (continuity of x ↦ P_x on M is assumed; in the parent it comes from the sibling node submanifold_tangent).

Notation. For x ∈ ℝᴺ: T_x := tangentSpace M x, ι_x : T_x → ℝᴺ the inclusion, π_x : ℝᴺ → T_x the orthogonal projection, P_x := tangentProjection M x = (T_x).starProjection = ι_x ∘ π_x, A_x := fderiv ℝ f x, L_x := A_x ∘ ι_x, J*f(x) := coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L_x L_x*).

1. (Pointwise identity, every x ∈ ℝᴺ.) The adjoint of a composition is the reversed composition of adjoints, so L_x* = ι_x* ∘ A_x*. The adjoint of the inclusion ι_x is π_x: for t ∈ T_x and v ∈ ℝᴺ, ⟨ι_x t, v⟩ = ⟨t, π_x v⟩ because v − π_x v ⊥ T_x. Hence L_x L_x* = A_x ∘ ι_x ∘ π_x ∘ A_x* = A_x ∘ P_x ∘ A_x*, and J*f(x) = √det(A_x ∘ P_x ∘ A_x*) for every x.
2. (Continuity of the ingredients on M.) (a) f is C¹ on the open set U, so x ↦ A_x = Df(x) is continuous on U, hence on M ⊆ U. (b) B ↦ B* is a linear isometry (ℝᴺ →L ℝᵐ) → (ℝᵐ →L ℝᴺ), hence continuous; so x ↦ A_x* is continuous on M. (c) x ↦ P_x is continuous on M by hypothesis. (d) Composition of continuous linear maps is a bounded bilinear operation, hence jointly continuous; so x ↦ A_x ∘ P_x ∘ A_x* is continuous on M. (e) det : (ℝᵐ →L ℝᵐ) → ℝ is continuous (finite dimension) and √ : ℝ → ℝ is continuous.
3. By steps 1 and 2, J*f agrees on all of ℝᴺ with √ ∘ det ∘ (x ↦ A_x ∘ P_x ∘ A_x*), which is continuous on M. Hence J*f is continuous on M. This is the first conjunct.
4. (Relative closedness.) Fix y ∈ ℝᵐ and let S_y := M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {x : J*f(x) = 0}. f is continuous on U (C¹ implies continuous), hence on M. Claim: every x ∈ M ∩ closure(S_y) lies in S_y. Indeed choose x_j ∈ S_y with x_j → x (ℝᴺ is a metric space). All x_j and x lie in M, and f and J*f are continuous on M, so f(x) = lim f(x_j) = y and J*f(x) = lim J*f(x_j) = 0; thus x ∈ S_y.
5. Put F := closure(S_y), a closed subset of ℝᴺ. Then M ∩ F = S_y: "⊇" because S_y ⊆ M and S_y ⊆ closure(S_y); "⊆" by step 4. This is the second conjunct, for every y. ∎
(Equivalent route used in the checked Lean code: by the characterization of continuity on a subset, continuousOn_iff_isClosed, there are closed F₁, F₂ with J*f⁻¹{0} ∩ M = F₁ ∩ M and f⁻¹{y} ∩ M = F₂ ∩ M; then F := F₁ ∩ F₂ satisfies M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ {J*f = 0} = M ∩ F by elementwise set algebra.)

subproblem.title: Rank criterion for the coarea Jacobian (J*f(x) = 0 iff rank df_x < m)
subproblem.statement: For all N, m ∈ ℕ, every set M ⊆ ℝᴺ, every map f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and every point x ∈ ℝᴺ (ℝᵖ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)): with T := tangentSpace M x and L_x := Df(x) ∘ ι_T : T → ℝᵐ (Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, ι_T the inclusion), coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L_x L_x*) equals 0 if and only if the dimension of range(L_x) = LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f x).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M x).subtype) is < m. No hypothesis on M or f is needed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N), coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ↔ Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f x).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M x).subtype)) < m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof of root.c1_sard-a1, PART II steps 1-2 (Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §6, p. 66: "J*f(x) ≠ 0 precisely when df_x has rank m"). This lemma is pure linear algebra; it holds at every point x, with no hypothesis on M or f.

Notation. Fix N, m ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and x ∈ ℝᴺ (ℝᵖ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)). T := tangentSpace M x is a linear subspace of ℝᴺ; with the restricted inner product it is a finite-dimensional (hence complete) inner product space. Let A := fderiv ℝ f x : ℝᴺ →L ℝᵐ (if f is not differentiable at x this is 0; no property of A is used below), ι : T → ℝᴺ the inclusion, L := A ∘ ι : T →L ℝᵐ, and L* : ℝᵐ →L T its adjoint, ⟨L* w, t⟩ = ⟨w, L t⟩. By definition coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L ∘ L*), where L ∘ L* : ℝᵐ → ℝᵐ. The underlying linear map of L is (fderiv ℝ f x).toLinearMap ∘ₗ T.subtype, so range L is exactly the submodule in the statement.

1. L L* is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite: ⟨L L* w, w⟩ = ⟨L* w, L* w⟩ = |L* w|² ≥ 0 for every w ∈ ℝᵐ. Hence its eigenvalues are ≥ 0 and det(L L*) ≥ 0.
2. Since Real.sqrt d = 0 iff d ≤ 0, step 1 gives: coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ⟺ det(L L*) ≤ 0 ⟺ det(L L*) = 0.
3. L L* is an endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ, so det(L L*) = 0 ⟺ L L* is not invertible ⟺ L L* is not injective.
4. L L* is not injective ⟺ there is w ≠ 0 with L L* w = 0 ⟺ there is w ≠ 0 with L* w = 0. (If L L* w = 0 then |L* w|² = ⟨L L* w, w⟩ = 0, so L* w = 0; conversely L* w = 0 gives L L* w = 0.) Thus L L* is not injective ⟺ ker L* ≠ {0}.
5. ker L* = (range L)^⊥: w ∈ ker L* ⟺ ⟨L* w, t⟩ = 0 for all t ∈ T ⟺ ⟨w, L t⟩ = 0 for all t ∈ T. In the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ, (range L)^⊥ = {0} ⟺ range L = ℝᵐ. Hence ker L* ≠ {0} ⟺ range L ≠ ℝᵐ, i.e. ⟺ L is not surjective.
6. dim ℝᵐ = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Every subspace of ℝᵐ has dimension ≤ m, and a subspace of dimension m is all of ℝᵐ; so range L ≠ ℝᵐ ⟺ finrank(range L) < m.
7. Chaining steps 2-6: coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ⟺ Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f x).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M x).subtype)) < m. As N, m, M, f, x were arbitrary, the statement holds. ∎

subproblem.title: Level sets of a C¹ submersion have Simon local representations (implicit function theorem)
subproblem.statement: Let m, k ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^{m+k} open, G : ℝ^{m+k} → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on V, and x₀ ∈ V with DG(x₀) = fderiv ℝ G x₀ surjective. Then there are D ⊆ ℝᵏ, V₁ ⊆ ℝ^{m+k} with x₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V, and l : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{m+k} such that IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (G⁻¹{G(x₀)}) D V₁ l: D and V₁ are open, l is C¹ and injective on D, l(D) = V₁ ∩ G⁻¹{G(x₀)}, D ∩ l⁻¹(Q) is compact for every compact Q ⊆ V₁, and Dl(z) is injective for all z ∈ D.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (G : Rn (m + k) → Rn m) (x₀ : Rn (m + k)), IsOpen V → x₀ ∈ V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G V → Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ G x₀) → ∃ (D : Set (Rn k)) (V₁ : Set (Rn (m + k))) (l : Rn k → Rn (m + k)), x₀ ∈ V₁ ∧ V₁ ⊆ V ∧ Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (G ⁻¹' {G x₀}) D V₁ l
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof of root.c1_sard-a1, PART II steps 7-10 (the inverse/implicit function theorem construction behind Simon's "the implicit function theorem implies that f⁻¹(y) \ C ... is a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold", p. 66-67), carried out in the parameter space for an arbitrary C¹ map G (in the parent G = f ∘ ψ). This lemma says that a level set of a C¹ map whose derivative is onto at x₀ has a C¹ Simon local representation near x₀ (Simon 4.1), inside any prescribed open V.

Notation. n := m + k, ℝᵖ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p), y₀ := G(x₀), A := fderiv ℝ G x₀ (surjective). ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ carries its product (sup) norm; it is a finite-dimensional normed space of dimension m + k.

1. (Kernel and complementary coordinate.) K := ker A ⊆ ℝⁿ. By rank-nullity, dim(range A) + dim K = n; range A = ℝᵐ by surjectivity, so dim K = n − m = k = dim ℝᵏ. Choose a linear isomorphism e : K → ℝᵏ (equal finite dimensions), let P_K : ℝⁿ → K be the orthogonal projection, and put π := e ∘ P_K : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ (continuous linear). For v ∈ K, P_K v = v, hence π v = e v.
2. (The map Φ.) Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ, Φ(x) := (G(x), π(x − x₀)). Φ is C¹ on V (first component by hypothesis, second affine), Φ(x₀) = (y₀, 0), and for x ∈ V (V open) Φ has derivative DΦ(x) = (DG(x), π).
3. (DΦ(x₀) is invertible.) (A, π) is injective: if A v = A w and π v = π w, then v − w ∈ K and e(v − w) = π(v − w) = 0, so v = w. As dim ℝⁿ = m + k = dim(ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ), the injective linear map (A, π) is bijective; let Φ' : ℝⁿ ≃L ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ be the resulting continuous linear equivalence, so Φ has derivative Φ' at x₀.
4. (Inverse function theorem.) Φ is C¹ at x₀ with invertible derivative Φ'. By the C¹ inverse function theorem there is a local homeomorphism h (an open partial homeomorphism ℝⁿ ⇀ ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) with h = Φ as functions, x₀ ∈ source(h), source and target open, h mapping source(h) bijectively onto target(h) with continuous inverse h⁻¹ (h⁻¹(h x) = x on the source, h(h⁻¹ ω) = ω on the target, h(source) ⊆ target, h⁻¹(target) ⊆ source).
5. (Restrict to invertible derivative.) V_inv := {x ∈ V : DΦ(x) is invertible} is open: x ↦ DΦ(x) is continuous on the open set V (Φ is C¹ on V) and the invertible continuous linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ form an open set. x₀ ∈ V_inv by step 3. Let h' be h restricted to V_inv: source(h') = source(h) ∩ V_inv ⊆ V, h' = Φ and h'⁻¹ = h⁻¹ as functions, and x₀ ∈ source(h').
6. (Regularity of the inverse.) Let ω ∈ target(h') and x := h'⁻¹(ω) ∈ source(h') ⊆ V_inv. Then DΦ(x) is (the underlying map of) a continuous linear equivalence E_ω and Φ is C¹ at x (x ∈ V). By the inverse-function regularity lemmas for local homeomorphisms, h'⁻¹ has derivative E_ω⁻¹ at ω and is C¹ at ω.
7. (Box and chart.) target(h') is open and contains Φ(x₀) = (y₀, 0). Choose ε > 0 with B((y₀,0), ε) ⊆ target(h'); in the product norm B((y₀,0), ε) = B(y₀, ε) × B(0, ε) =: O. Define D := B(0, ε) ⊆ ℝᵏ (open ball), V₁ := source(h') ∩ Φ⁻¹(O) (open, since source(h') is open and Φ = h' is continuous on it), j(z) := (y₀, z), and l(z) := h'⁻¹(y₀, z) for z ∈ ℝᵏ. For z ∈ D, j(z) ∈ O ⊆ target(h').
8. (x₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V.) x₀ ∈ source(h') and Φ(x₀) = (y₀, 0) ∈ O; V₁ ⊆ source(h') ⊆ V.
9. (Openness.) D and V₁ are open (step 7).
10. (C¹ on D.) For z ∈ D, l = h'⁻¹ ∘ j, j is affine (C^∞) and h'⁻¹ is C¹ at j(z) ∈ target(h') (step 6); so l is C¹ at z. Hence l is C¹ on D.
11. (Injective on D.) If z, z' ∈ D and l(z) = l(z'), applying h' and h'(h'⁻¹ ω) = ω gives (y₀, z) = (y₀, z'), so z = z'.
12. (Image.) l(D) = V₁ ∩ G⁻¹{y₀}. (⊆) For z ∈ D, ω := (y₀, z) ∈ target(h'), so x := l(z) = h'⁻¹(ω) ∈ source(h') and Φ(x) = h'(h'⁻¹ ω) = ω ∈ O; thus x ∈ V₁, and G(x) = (first component of Φ(x)) = y₀. (⊇) If x ∈ V₁ and G(x) = y₀, then Φ(x) = (y₀, π(x − x₀)) ∈ O, so z := π(x − x₀) ∈ B(0, ε) = D, and l(z) = h'⁻¹(Φ(x)) = h'⁻¹(h'(x)) = x since x ∈ source(h').
13. (Properness relative to (D, V₁).) Let Q ⊆ V₁ be compact. Φ is continuous on V₁ ⊆ V, so Φ(Q) is compact. Claim: D ∩ l⁻¹(Q) = j⁻¹(Φ(Q)) = {z : (y₀, z) ∈ Φ(Q)}. (⊆) If z ∈ D and l(z) ∈ Q then (y₀, z) = h'(h'⁻¹(y₀, z)) = Φ(l(z)) ∈ Φ(Q). (⊇) If (y₀, z) = Φ(q) with q ∈ Q ⊆ V₁, then Φ(q) ∈ O gives z ∈ B(0, ε) = D, and l(z) = h'⁻¹(Φ(q)) = h'⁻¹(h'(q)) = q ∈ Q because q ∈ source(h'). Now j⁻¹(Φ(Q)) is closed (Φ(Q) is compact hence closed, j continuous) and contained in the compact set pr₂(Φ(Q)); a closed subset of a compact set is compact. Hence D ∩ l⁻¹(Q) is compact.
14. (Injective derivative.) For z ∈ D, by the chain rule Dl(z) = D(h'⁻¹)(j(z)) ∘ Dj(z) = E⁻¹ ∘ (h ↦ (0, h)), with E the equivalence from step 6 at ω = j(z). Both factors are injective, so Dl(z) is injective.
15. Steps 8-14 give x₀ ∈ V₁, V₁ ⊆ V and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (G⁻¹{G x₀}) D V₁ l: IsOpen D, IsOpen V₁, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 l D, InjOn l D, l '' D = V₁ ∩ G⁻¹{G x₀}, IsProperOnInto l D V₁, and Dl(z) injective for z ∈ D. ∎
(Edge cases: k = 0 gives ℝᵏ = {0}, K = {0}, D = {0}; m = 0 gives A trivially onto, K = ℝⁿ. No step assumes m > 0 or k > 0.)

```lean
theorem c1_sard_submersion_level_set_chart : ∀ (m k : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (G : Rn (m + k) → Rn m) (x₀ : Rn (m + k)), IsOpen V → x₀ ∈ V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G V → Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ G x₀) → ∃ (D : Set (Rn k)) (V₁ : Set (Rn (m + k))) (l : Rn k → Rn (m + k)), x₀ ∈ V₁ ∧ V₁ ⊆ V ∧ Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (G ⁻¹' {G x₀}) D V₁ l := by
  intro m k V G x₀ hV hx₀ hG hsurj
  -- kernel of A and a complementary map π
  set A : Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn m := fderiv ℝ G x₀ with hA
  set K : Submodule ℝ (Rn (m + k)) := LinearMap.ker (A : Rn (m + k) →ₗ[ℝ] Rn m) with hK
  have hrange : LinearMap.range (A : Rn (m + k) →ₗ[ℝ] Rn m) = ⊤ := LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hsurj
  have hKdim : Module.finrank ℝ K = Module.finrank ℝ (Rn k) := by
    have h := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker (A : Rn (m + k) →ₗ[ℝ] Rn m)
    rw [hrange, finrank_top, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, ← hK] at h
    rw [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]
    omega
  let e : K ≃ₗ[ℝ] Rn k := LinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq K (Rn k) hKdim
  let π : Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn k :=
    (e.toContinuousLinearEquiv : K →L[ℝ] Rn k) ∘L K.orthogonalProjectionOnto
  have hπK : ∀ v : K, π v = e v := by
    intro v
    simp [π]
  -- the map Φ
  let Φ : Rn (m + k) → Rn m × Rn k := fun x => (G x, π (x - x₀))
  have hπaff : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x : Rn (m + k) => π (x - x₀)) :=
    π.contDiff.comp (contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const)
  have hΦC : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ V := hG.prodMk hπaff.contDiffOn
  have hΦCA : ∀ x ∈ V, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 Φ x := fun x hx => hΦC.contDiffAt (hV.mem_nhds hx)
  have hπd : ∀ x, HasFDerivAt (fun x : Rn (m + k) => π (x - x₀)) π x := by
    intro x
    have h1 : HasFDerivAt (fun x : Rn (m + k) => x - x₀) (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Rn (m + k))) x :=
      (hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const x₀
    have h2 := (π.hasFDerivAt (x := x - x₀)).comp x h1
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_id] at h2
    exact h2
  have hΦd : ∀ x ∈ V, HasFDerivAt Φ ((fderiv ℝ G x).prod π) x := by
    intro x hx
    have hGx : HasFDerivAt G (fderiv ℝ G x) x :=
      ((hG.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hV.mem_nhds hx)).hasFDerivAt
    exact hGx.prodMk (hπd x)

  have hinj : Function.Injective (A.prod π) := by
    intro v w hvw
    have h1 : A v = A w := congrArg Prod.fst hvw
    have h2 : π v = π w := congrArg Prod.snd hvw
    have hmem : v - w ∈ K := by
      show A (v - w) = 0
      rw [map_sub, h1, sub_self]
    have h3 : e ⟨v - w, hmem⟩ = e 0 := by
      rw [← hπK, map_zero]
      show π (v - w) = 0
      rw [map_sub, h2, sub_self]
    have := congrArg Subtype.val (e.injective h3)
    simpa [sub_eq_zero] using this
  have hdim : Module.finrank ℝ (Rn (m + k)) = Module.finrank ℝ (Rn m × Rn k) := by
    rw [Module.finrank_prod, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin,
      finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]
  have hsurjΦ : Function.Surjective (A.prod π) :=
    (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank hdim).mp hinj
  let Φ' : Rn (m + k) ≃L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k :=
    (LinearEquiv.ofBijective ((A.prod π : Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k) :
      Rn (m + k) →ₗ[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k) ⟨hinj, hsurjΦ⟩).toContinuousLinearEquiv
  have hΦ'd : HasFDerivAt Φ (Φ' : Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k) x₀ := by
    have : (Φ' : Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k) = A.prod π := by ext1 v; rfl
    rw [this]; exact hΦd x₀ hx₀

  let h := (hΦCA x₀ hx₀).toOpenPartialHomeomorph Φ hΦ'd one_ne_zero
  have hh : (h : Rn (m + k) → Rn m × Rn k) = Φ := rfl
  -- the open set where DΦ is invertible
  set Vinv : Set (Rn (m + k)) := V ∩ (fderiv ℝ Φ) ⁻¹'
    (range ((↑) : (Rn (m + k) ≃L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k) → Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k)) with hVinv
  have hVinvo : IsOpen Vinv :=
    (hΦC.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen hV le_rfl).isOpen_inter_preimage hV
      ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen

  have hh' : (h' : Rn (m + k) → Rn m × Rn k) = Φ := rfl
  have hx₀src : x₀ ∈ h'.source :=
    ⟨(hΦCA x₀ hx₀).mem_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source hΦ'd one_ne_zero, hx₀inv⟩
  have hsrcV : h'.source ⊆ V := fun x hx => hx.2.1
  have hΦx₀ : Φ x₀ = (G x₀, 0) := by simp [Φ]
  have htgt : (G x₀, (0 : Rn k)) ∈ h'.target := by
    rw [← hΦx₀, ← hh']; exact h'.map_source hx₀src
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hball⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.mp h'.open_target _ htgt
  set O : Set (Rn m × Rn k) := ball (G x₀) ε ×ˢ ball (0 : Rn k) ε with hO
  have hOt : O ⊆ h'.target := by rw [hO, ball_prod_same]; exact hball
  have hjO : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : Rn k) ε, ((G x₀, z) : Rn m × Rn k) ∈ O :=
    fun z hz => ⟨mem_ball_self hε, hz⟩
  have hsymm : ∀ ω ∈ h'.target, ∃ eqv : Rn (m + k) ≃L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k,
      HasFDerivAt h'.symm (eqv.symm : Rn m × Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn (m + k)) ω ∧
        ContDiffAt ℝ 1 h'.symm ω := by
    intro ω hω
    have hxs : h'.symm ω ∈ h'.source := h'.map_target hω
    obtain ⟨eqv, heqv⟩ := hxs.2.2
    have hxV : h'.symm ω ∈ V := hxs.2.1
    have hd : HasFDerivAt h' (eqv : Rn (m + k) →L[ℝ] Rn m × Rn k) (h'.symm ω) := by
      rw [heqv]; exact ((hΦCA _ hxV).differentiableAt one_ne_zero).hasFDerivAt
    exact ⟨eqv, h'.hasFDerivAt_symm hω hd, h'.contDiffAt_symm hω hd (hΦCA _ hxV)⟩
  refine ⟨ball (0 : Rn k) ε, h'.source ∩ Φ ⁻¹' O, fun z => h'.symm (G x₀, z),
    ⟨hx₀src, ?_⟩, fun x hx => hsrcV hx.1, ?_⟩
  · rw [Set.mem_preimage, hΦx₀]; exact ⟨mem_ball_self hε, mem_ball_self hε⟩
  refine ⟨isOpen_ball, h'.isOpen_inter_preimage (isOpen_ball.prod isOpen_ball), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- C¹
    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨eqv, -, hcd⟩ := hsymm _ (hOt (hjO z hz))
    exact (hcd.comp z (contDiffAt_const.prodMk contDiffAt_id)).contDiffWithinAt
  · -- injective
    intro z hz z' hz' hzz
    have h1 := h'.right_inv (hOt (hjO z hz))
    have h2 := h'.right_inv (hOt (hjO z' hz'))
    have := congrArg h' hzz
    simp only at this
    rw [h1, h2] at this
    exact (Prod.mk.inj this).2
  · -- image
    ext x
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩
      have hω := hOt (hjO z hz)
      refine ⟨⟨h'.map_target hω, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
      · show Φ (h'.symm (G x₀, z)) ∈ O
        rw [← hh', h'.right_inv hω]; exact hjO z hz
      · show G (h'.symm (G x₀, z)) = G x₀
        exact congrArg Prod.fst (h'.right_inv hω)
    · rintro ⟨⟨hxs, hxO⟩, hxG⟩
      have hxG' : G x = G x₀ := hxG
      refine ⟨π (x - x₀), hxO.2, ?_⟩
      show h'.symm (G x₀, π (x - x₀)) = x
      have : ((G x₀, π (x - x₀)) : Rn m × Rn k) = h' x := by rw [hh']; simp [Φ, hxG']
      rw [this, h'.left_inv hxs]
  · -- proper
    intro Q hQ hQV₁
    have hΦQ : IsCompact (Φ '' Q) :=
      hQ.image_of_continuousOn (hΦC.continuousOn.mono (fun x hx => hsrcV (hQV₁ hx).1))
    have heq : ball (0 : Rn k) ε ∩ (fun z => h'.symm (G x₀, z)) ⁻¹' Q =
        (fun z : Rn k => ((G x₀, z) : Rn m × Rn k)) ⁻¹' (Φ '' Q) := by
      ext z
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hz, hzQ⟩
        refine ⟨_, hzQ, ?_⟩
        rw [← hh', h'.right_inv (hOt (hjO z hz))]
      · rintro ⟨q, hq, hqz⟩
        have hqz' : Φ q = (G x₀, z) := hqz
        have hqO : Φ q ∈ O := (hQV₁ hq).2

        refine ⟨hqO.2, ?_⟩

        rw [← hqz', ← hh', h'.left_inv (hQV₁ hq).1]; exact hq

    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨eqv, hd, -⟩ := hsymm _ (hOt (hjO z hz))
    have hj : HasFDerivAt (fun z : Rn k => ((G x₀, z) : Rn m × Rn k))

      h'.symm ∘ (fun z : Rn k => ((G x₀, z) : Rn m × Rn k)) from rfl, hcomp.fderiv,
      ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp]
```

proof_key_steps: K = ker DG(x₀) has dimension k; set π := e ∘ P_K with e : K ≅ ℝᵏ.
Φ(x) = (G(x), π(x − x₀)) is C¹ on V and DΦ(x₀) = (DG(x₀), π) is injective, hence an isomorphism.
Inverse function theorem: a local homeomorphism h = Φ near x₀, restricted to the open set where DΦ is invertible, so h⁻¹ is C¹ with invertible derivative on its target.
Choose a box B(G x₀, ε) × B(0, ε) in the target; D := B(0, ε), V₁ := source ∩ Φ⁻¹(box), l(z) := h⁻¹(G x₀, z).
Check the clauses: l is C¹ and injective, l(D) = V₁ ∩ G⁻¹{G x₀}, properness (D ∩ l⁻¹Q is a closed slice of the compact Φ(Q)), and Dl(z) = (DΦ)⁻¹ ∘ (0, ·) is injective.

subproblem.title: The regular part of every fiber is a k-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold
subproblem.statement: Let N, m, k ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ an (m+k)-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open with M ⊆ U, and f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on U. Assume (i) for every C¹ Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of M with ψ : ℝ^{m+k} → ℝᴺ and every x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x); and (ii) x ↦ coareaJacobian M f x is continuous on M. Then for every y ∈ ℝᵐ, (M ∩ f⁻¹{y}) \ {x : coareaJacobian M f x = 0} is a k-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ (IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝᵏ) 1; vacuously if it is empty).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn (m + k)) 1 M → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → (∀ (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn (m + k) → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) → ContinuousOn (coareaJacobian M f) M → ∀ y : Rn m, Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn k) 1 ((M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) \ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof of root.c1_sard-a1, PART II steps 6, 7 and 11 (Simon, Ch. 2 §6, p. 66-67: "since J*f(x) ≠ 0 precisely when df_x has rank m, the implicit function theorem implies that either f⁻¹(y) \ C is empty or else it is a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold"). The construction is delegated to the sibling lemmas jacobian_rank (c1_sard_coarea_jacobian_eq_zero_iff), level_set_chart (c1_sard_submersion_level_set_chart) and chart_composition (c1_sard_local_representation_comp). Hypothesis (i) (tangent space = range of the chart derivative) and hypothesis (ii) (continuity of J*f on M) are supplied in the parent by the sibling nodes submanifold_tangent and jacobian_continuity.

Fix y ∈ ℝᵐ and write Z := {x : J*f(x) = 0}, Σ := (M ∩ f⁻¹{y}) \ Z. By definition IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝᵏ) 1 Σ means: 1 ≤ 1 (true), and every p ∈ Σ has (D, W₁, φ) with p ∈ W₁ and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 Σ D W₁ φ, φ : ℝᵏ → ℝᴺ. (If Σ = ∅ the second clause is vacuous.) Fix p ∈ Σ, so p ∈ M, f(p) = y and J*f(p) ≠ 0.

1. (Chart of M at p.) M is an (m+k)-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold and p ∈ M, so there are V ⊆ ℝ^{m+k}, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ with p ∈ W and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ. Since p ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), p = ψ(x_p) for some x_p ∈ V. Also ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M ⊆ U.
2. (Regular region of the chart.) V' := {x ∈ V : J*f(ψ(x)) ≠ 0}. J*f ∘ ψ is continuous on V (ψ is continuous on V and maps V into M, and J*f is continuous on M by (ii)) and V is open, so V' = V ∩ (J*f ∘ ψ)⁻¹(ℝ \ {0}) is open. x_p ∈ V' because J*f(p) ≠ 0.
3. (G := f ∘ ψ is C¹ on V'.) f is C¹ on U, ψ is C¹ on V ⊇ V', and ψ(V') ⊆ M ⊆ U; hence G is C¹ on V'.
4. (DG(x_p) is surjective.) Let T := tangentSpace M p and L := Df(p) ∘ ι_T. By jacobian_rank, J*f(p) = 0 ⟺ finrank(range L) < m; as J*f(p) ≠ 0, finrank(range L) ≥ m, and since range L ⊆ ℝᵐ with dim ℝᵐ = m, range L = ℝᵐ. So for w ∈ ℝᵐ there is t ∈ T with Df(p) t = w. By (i), T = range Dψ(x_p), so t = Dψ(x_p) v for some v ∈ ℝ^{m+k}. f is differentiable at p (p ∈ U open, f C¹ on U) and ψ is differentiable at x_p (x_p ∈ V open, ψ C¹ on V); by the chain rule DG(x_p) = Df(p) ∘ Dψ(x_p), so DG(x_p) v = Df(p) t = w. Hence DG(x_p) is surjective.
5. (Slice chart in the parameter space.) level_set_chart applied to m, k, the open set V', G and x₀ := x_p (x_p ∈ V', G C¹ on V', DG(x_p) onto) gives D ⊆ ℝᵏ, V₁ with x_p ∈ V₁ ⊆ V', and l : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{m+k} with IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (G⁻¹{G(x_p)}) D V₁ l. Here G(x_p) = f(p) = y.
6. (Change of represented set.) V₁ ∩ G⁻¹{y} = V₁ ∩ ψ⁻¹(Σ): for x ∈ V₁ ⊆ V' ⊆ V we have ψ(x) ∈ M and J*f(ψ(x)) ≠ 0, hence ψ(x) ∈ Σ ⟺ f(ψ(x)) = y ⟺ G(x) = y. Since IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 X D V₁ l depends on X only through its image clause l(D) = V₁ ∩ X, also IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (ψ⁻¹(Σ)) D V₁ l.
7. (Composition.) chart_composition applied to n := m + k, k, N, M, S := Σ (Σ ⊆ M), the representation (V, W, ψ) of M, V₁ ⊆ V (V₁ ⊆ V' ⊆ V) and the representation (D, V₁, l) of ψ⁻¹(Σ) gives W₁ ⊆ W with ψ(V₁) = W₁ ∩ M and IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 Σ D W₁ (ψ ∘ l).
8. (p ∈ W₁.) p = ψ(x_p) with x_p ∈ V₁, so p ∈ ψ(V₁) = W₁ ∩ M; hence p ∈ W₁.
9. Steps 1-8 give, for each p ∈ Σ, a C¹ Simon local representation (D, W₁, ψ ∘ l) of Σ with parameter space ℝᵏ and p ∈ W₁; with 1 ≤ 1 this is IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝᵏ) 1 Σ. As y was arbitrary, the statement holds. ∎

```lean
theorem c1_sard_regular_fiber_submanifold : ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn (m + k)) 1 M → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → (∀ (V : Set (Rn (m + k))) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn (m + k) → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) → ContinuousOn (coareaJacobian M f) M → ∀ y : Rn m, Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn k) 1 ((M ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) \ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0}) := by
  intro N m k M U f hM hU hMU hf htan hJ y
  refine ⟨le_rfl, ?_⟩
  intro p hp
  obtain ⟨⟨hpM, hpy⟩, hpZ⟩ := hp
  have hpy' : f p = y := hpy
  have hpZ' : coareaJacobian M f p ≠ 0 := hpZ
  obtain ⟨V, W, ψ, hpW, hψ⟩ := hM.2 p hpM
  have hpimg : p ∈ ψ '' V := by rw [hψ.image_eq]; exact ⟨hpW, hpM⟩
  obtain ⟨xp, hxpV, rfl⟩ := hpimg
  subst hpy'
  have hψM : MapsTo ψ V M := fun x hx => by
    have : ψ x ∈ ψ '' V := ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    rw [hψ.image_eq] at this; exact this.2
  set V' : Set (Rn (m + k)) := V ∩ (coareaJacobian M f ∘ ψ) ⁻¹' {0}ᶜ with hV'def
  have hV'open : IsOpen V' :=
    (hJ.comp hψ.contDiffOn.continuousOn hψM).isOpen_inter_preimage hψ.isOpen_source isOpen_compl_singleton
  have hV'V : V' ⊆ V := inter_subset_left
  have hxpV' : xp ∈ V' := ⟨hxpV, hpZ'⟩
  have hG : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (f ∘ ψ) V' :=
    hf.comp (hψ.contDiffOn.mono hV'V) (fun x hx => hMU (hψM (hV'V hx)))
  have hdf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (ψ xp) :=
    (hf.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hU.mem_nhds (hMU hpM))
  have hdψ : DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ xp :=
    (hψ.contDiffOn.differentiableOn one_ne_zero).differentiableAt (hψ.isOpen_source.mem_nhds hxpV)
  have hsurjL : LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f (ψ xp)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M (ψ xp)).subtype) = ⊤ := by
    have h1 := (c1_sard_coarea_jacobian_eq_zero_iff N m M f (ψ xp)).not.mp hpZ'
    apply Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq
    have h2 := Submodule.finrank_le (LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f (ψ xp)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M (ψ xp)).subtype))
    rw [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin] at h2 ⊢
    omega
  have hsurjG : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) xp) := by
    intro w
    have hw : w ∈ LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f (ψ xp)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M (ψ xp)).subtype) := by
      rw [hsurjL]; trivial
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hw
    have htmem : (t : Rn N) ∈ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ xp).toLinearMap := by
      rw [← htan V W ψ hψ xp hxpV]; exact t.2
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := htmem
    refine ⟨v, ?_⟩
    rw [fderiv_comp xp hdf hdψ]
    have hv' : fderiv ℝ ψ xp v = t := hv
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp', Function.comp_apply, hv']
    simpa using ht
  obtain ⟨D, V₁, l, hxpV₁, hV₁V', hl⟩ :=
    c1_sard_submersion_level_set_chart m k V' (f ∘ ψ) xp hV'open hxpV' hG hsurjG
  set S : Set (Rn N) := (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {f (ψ xp)}) \ {x | coareaJacobian M f x = 0} with hSdef
  have hset : V₁ ∩ (f ∘ ψ) ⁻¹' {(f ∘ ψ) xp} = V₁ ∩ ψ ⁻¹' S := by
    ext x
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hx1, hx2⟩
      have hxV' := hV₁V' hx1
      exact ⟨hx1, ⟨hψM hxV'.1, hx2⟩, hxV'.2⟩
    · rintro ⟨hx1, ⟨_, hx2⟩, _⟩
      exact ⟨hx1, hx2⟩
  have hl' : Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 (ψ ⁻¹' S) D V₁ l := by
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7⟩ := hl
    exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, h5.trans hset, h6, h7⟩
  have hSM : S ⊆ M := fun x hx => hx.1.1
  obtain ⟨W₁, hW₁W, hW₁img, hrep⟩ :=
    c1_sard_local_representation_comp (m + k) k N M S V W ψ D V₁ l hψ hSM (hV₁V'.trans hV'V) hl'
  have hpW₁ : ψ xp ∈ W₁ := by
    have : ψ xp ∈ ψ '' V₁ := ⟨xp, hxpV₁, rfl⟩
    rw [hW₁img] at this; exact this.1
  exact ⟨D, W₁, ψ ∘ l, hpW₁, hrep⟩
```

proof_key_steps: Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of M at p = ψ(x_p); V' := {x ∈ V : J*f(ψ x) ≠ 0} is open and contains x_p.
G := f ∘ ψ is C¹ on V', and DG(x_p) = Df(p) ∘ Dψ(x_p) is surjective by jacobian_rank and T_pM = range Dψ(x_p).
level_set_chart gives (D, V₁, l) for G⁻¹{y} with x_p ∈ V₁ ⊆ V'; on V₁, G⁻¹{y} = ψ⁻¹(Σ_y).
chart_composition gives W₁ with ψ(V₁) = W₁ ∩ M and (D, W₁, ψ ∘ l) a Simon chart of Σ_y with p ∈ W₁.
